solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loudmouth baronet trapping fish with bait

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece closes around the others

parts.note: Bt is the standard abbreviation after a baronet's name
short for ragworm, which anglers use as bait
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A noisy titled gentleman goes fishing with a net and a bucket of bait.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation BT opens up to hold RAG and GAR side by side, giving B-RAG-GAR-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart boasts loudly about himself, which is exactly what a loudmouth does; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Preacher: no point looking toward Heaven?

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing skyward means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: an old word of refusal
the nub is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: A preacher who has lost his point gazes upward for inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon separates the definition from the wordplay; NAY and NUB are joined and then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan, the seventeenth-century author of The Pilgrim's Progress, was a Nonconformist minister famous for his sermons.

clue.text: Medium interest in following sentence?

parts.note: coming after, following on
a life sentence, in prison slang simply 'life'

explanation.surface: Someone of middling curiosity waits to hear the next line of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like an adjective meaning moderate; it is the noun, a spiritualist who contacts the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualist mediums claim to pass messages from the dead, so existence beyond death is their chief concern.

clue.text: Try to cage rook that hurt amusing brother

indicators.note: a cage encloses whatever is put in it, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: to have a go is to have a try
R is the chess notation for a rook
the cry you give when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lock up a bird, and the pain of it makes a jokey sibling cry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the bird in a cage; it is the chess piece. 'That hurt' stands for the cry of pain itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the best known of the Marx Brothers, the American film comedy family, famed for his wisecracks.

clue.text: Cook in oven or pan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cook meat by dry heat in an oven
second meaning: criticise savagely, as a reviewer does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' reads as the cooking vessel alongside the oven, but it is the verb for giving a harsh review.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both baking meat with dry heat and mocking or criticising someone mercilessly.

clue.text: US city rents in recession increase continually

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the letters retreat and read backward

parts.note: Los Angeles
rents here are tears in cloth

explanation.surface: Housing costs in an American city keep climbing even as the economy shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' looks like housing costs and 'recession' like an economic slump; rents are rips and recession means going backward.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that spiral keep rising faster and faster, winding upward without stopping, as in an inflationary spiral.

clue.text: A person is fitted with one in old age

parts.note: as in 'a pound a head', meaning per head

indicators.note: something fitted with a part has that part set inside it

parts.note: a man is a person
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly person is given a new part, such as a replacement hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old age' suggests being elderly; here it is a geological age. 'A' becomes PER, as in 'ten pence a go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Permian is a period of geological time roughly 300 to 250 million years ago, so a very ancient era.

clue.text: What to do when in power shower we hear?

definitions.text: What to do when in power

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, not a spelling, so the word is swapped for one pronounced identically

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: A question about what to do in a power shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power shower' reads as a single bathroom fitting; split it, and 'power' belongs to the definition while 'shower' is the sound source.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch in power is said to rule over the country, and doing so for a period is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Story by Bavarian? Not right for loyal servant

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave out the letter that stands for right

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
Bavaria is a region of Germany
places the pieces next to each other

explanation.surface: A folk tale from Bavaria is praised as fit for a faithful retainer.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the usual abbreviation for right, is dropped from GERMAN, leaving GEMAN after LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a liegeman was a vassal sworn to serve his lord faithfully, so a devoted retainer.

clue.text: Bring trouble upon oneself when tackle catches pro

parts.note: as in 'as I arrived', meaning when

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: tackle is equipment, as is kit
to be pro something is to be for it

explanation.surface: A fisherman's gear snags a professional angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' suggests a professional; it is the Latin-derived word meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for it is an idiom for behaving so that punishment or misfortune seems deserved.

clue.text: Unsettled Irish cannot leave: hard to evade conscription!

indicators.note: unsettled things are disturbed and out of place, so the letters get rearranged
whatever evades the group escapes it, so that letter goes missing

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Restless Irish youths are told they cannot leave the country to dodge the draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like part of the story about emigrating, but it is fodder; only the H is dropped before the fifteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: National service was compulsory military duty for young men in Britain until 1960, a form of the draft.

clue.text: Inside a belly's endlessly delicious fruit

indicators.note: one thing inside another means it is placed within it

parts.note: taken as written
a pot belly is a round stomach

indicators.note: without an end, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: rich food is luscious and delicious

explanation.surface: Something tasty lies inside someone's stomach after a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belly' is a noun here, as in a pot belly, not the stomach contents the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Criminal bagging top-quality earthenware

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods
A1 means first-rate, with the numeral written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with the finest pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is often written AI in crosswords, the digit one looking like the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is glazed decorated pottery, originally from Faenza in Italy, a type of fired clay ware.

clue.text: Greek character involved in slight makes Cretan cross

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up within it

parts.note: slight and minor both mean small or unimportant
the Greek letter T

explanation.surface: A Greek man drawn into a small snub angers someone from Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective for angry; it is the noun for a hybrid creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of Greek myth, half man and half bull, lived in the labyrinth on Crete, so a hybrid beast.

clue.text: For Lily a special house key

parts.note: taken as written
a standard abbreviation for special
a standard abbreviation for house
the Delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone named Lily is given a special key to a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' is capitalised so it reads as a girl's name; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a plant of the lily family, the flower of the Elysian Fields in Greek myth.

clue.text: Bounder's place over in North America

indicators.note: sitting in something means being enclosed by it

parts.note: the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: turned over, the word is flipped to read the other way

parts.note: to lay something down is to place it

explanation.surface: A cad's home is somewhere across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is British slang for a cad; here it is literally something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a southern African antelope, and antelopes move in leaps, so it is a jumping animal.

clue.text: Turkish area in grip of national rioting

indicators.note: held in a grip means clasped inside something
a riot is disorder, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A region of Turkey is gripped by rioting across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of NATIONAL close around A just before the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the Asian peninsula that forms most of Turkey, so the adjective describes Turkish land and people.

clue.text: Applause? I contribute to it, ousting Liberal in contest

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so a letter is removed
contributing to something means becoming part of it, going inside

parts.note: a round of clapping
taken as written
the standard abbreviation for Liberal; this letter goes

explanation.surface: An audience member is proud to join the clapping once a politician is voted out.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into HANDCLAP and the L is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a race or competition in which stronger entrants carry weights or penalties to even the odds.

clue.text: King getting into Great British bitter

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: ace is slang for great
R is short for rex, Latin for king
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The monarch starts drinking a pint of British beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great British' reads as one phrase; it splits into ACE and B, with R going between. Bitter is a British style of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rarer form of acerbic, meaning sour or harsh in taste or manner.

clue.text: New union member's restraining order for dullard

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a newly married woman, one partner in a fresh marriage
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A recruit to a trade union gets a court order against a dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union and 'restraining order' a court order; the union is a marriage and the order an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide, named after the sedative, is a tiresome person who speaks in platitudes, so a bore.

clue.text: Bones in head extremely logical, each round

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: brought round, the letters turn to face the other way

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Someone's skull shows an orderly mind, each bone rounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones in head' looks like the skull; 'in' only links, and the bones are elsewhere in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Patellae is the Latin plural of patella, the kneecap, so these are the bones at the front of the knees.

clue.text: Crescent shape clear in old stringed instrument

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a plucked instrument of the Renaissance
to clear a profit is to net it

explanation.surface: A curved shape shows up clearly on an antique lute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' means net as in taking home a sum after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette, from French for little moon, is a half-moon shaped space or object, as above a door.

clue.text: Go-between crushed spirit of resistance

parts.note: broke is the past tense of break, to crush
R, the physics symbol for resistance, stands for its essence

explanation.surface: A mediator breaks the will of a rebel movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushed spirit' reads as one phrase; it splits, with 'spirit of resistance' reduced to the symbol for electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker negotiates deals between buyers and sellers, acting as an agent in the middle.

clue.text: Old boy back to fill face with duck and game

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it

parts.note: a clock's face is its dial

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters the other way

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for a former pupil
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A former pupil returns to stuff his face with roast duck and game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like meat to go with the duck; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a two-headed spool is spun and tossed on a string held between two sticks.

clue.text: Virgin martyr gets on train finally coming in

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: someone who gets on grows older, or ages

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A saintly woman boards a train at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets on' suggests boarding; it means getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Agnes of Rome was a young Christian girl executed for her faith, venerated as a virgin martyr.

clue.text: Sense of grievance private soldier voiced

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out, so the word is replaced by its sound

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier from the ranks rather than an officer

explanation.surface: A private soldier speaks up about a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep, lasting resentment, the bitter feeling of having been wronged.

clue.text: Senior academic mostly giving one side of story?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the head of certain colleges and universities

explanation.surface: A top professor tells only his half of the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One side of story' suggests a biased account; the question mark flags a literal side of a page in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, or the front of a leaf, so a printed side.

clue.text: Secret fear at the end trapped in credit fraud

parts.note: a secret shared in confidence

indicators.note: something trapped in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: buying on tick means buying on credit

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A hidden dread that you'll finally be caught up in a credit card scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is informal British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence trick is a swindle in which the victim's trust is won and then exploited, a kind of scam.

clue.text: Imitation gem left in delicate shade

parts.note: paste is glass used to make fake jewels
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A fake jewel is set in a soft, subtle colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as setting the gem in a colour, but it only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastel colours are soft, pale tints such as baby blue or pale pink, light and subtle hues.

clue.text: Commander vacillating over Norwegian sector

indicators.note: a sector is a section cut from something larger, so the letters are a slice of the text

parts.note: letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A military leader dithers over a stretch of Norwegian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacillating' looks like an anagram signal; it is only the start of the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is a person in charge, a ruler or head of an institution, colony or state.
